canonical_title: The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Volume 4 of The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, this collection gathers short and medium-length fiction written between 1954 and 1964, including previously unpublished pieces, and features an introduction by James Tiptree, Jr.
page_summary:
Volume 4 of The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, this collection gathers short and medium-length fiction written between 1954 and 1964, including previously unpublished pieces, and features an introduction by James Tiptree, Jr. (Alice Sheldon) that opens with the question 'How do you know you're reading Philip K. Dick?' and identifies strangeness as the pervasive quality that first drew her to his work. Stories in the volume include 'Service Call,' 'Stand By,' 'The Days of Perky Pat,' and the title story 'The Minority Report,' later adapted as Steven Spielberg's 2002 film starring Tom Cruise.

**Why it matters.** James Tiptree, Jr.'s introduction -- itself written by one of science fiction's most celebrated writers -- offers a valuable secondary-source characterization of what makes Dick's fiction distinctively strange, and the volume's title story's film adaptation is one of the most commercially successful Dick adaptations to date.

*This entry documents the anthology as a publishing object; readers seeking analysis of the individual stories, including 'The Minority Report' itself, should consult each story's own dossier.*
